scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: A single IT Department workstation, it_lab3 (192.168.1.x),
"is totally isolated" -- the user says it can't reach anything at all, not even its
own gateway, and suspects the machine lost its network or its switch port died.
Please find and confirm the fault on it_lab3 and tell us what to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the host DNS resolver on it_lab3. Mechanism: it_lab3 can reach the LAN and remote subnets by IP, but all hostname lookups fail, which makes apps appear “offline.” Evidence: from it_lab3, ICMP to the default gateway 192.168.1.1 and a peer 192.168.1.3 succeeds, ARP entries are REACHABLE, eth0 is UP with correct IP/route, and pings to other subnets by IP also succeed. However, DNS fails: getent/ping example.com returns FAIL_DNS, and /etc/resolv.conf is an empty, zero‑byte regular file with wrong mode (-rwxr-xr-x 0), not the normal resolver content or symlink.

Localization: this is isolated to it_lab3 (192.168.1.5), interface eth0. There is no switch or link issue: link is detected, ARP works, and routing is correct.

Root cause: /etc/resolv.conf on it_lab3 was truncated to an empty regular file (not a symlink), leaving the host with no configured DNS servers.

Corrective fix: restore a valid resolver and, if using systemd-resolved, restart it. On it_lab3:
- Option A (simple static resolvers, no restart needed):
  rm -f /etc/resolv.conf
  printf 'nameserver 1.1.1.1\nnameserver 8.8.8.8\n' > /etc/resolv.conf
  chmod 644 /etc/resolv.conf
- Option B (systemd-resolved):
  rm -f /etc/resolv.conf
  ln -s /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf
  systemctl restart systemd-resolved

After this, DNS lookups should work and applications will regain connectivity. No switch or port restart is required.
